questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L01_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A survey asks students how many minutes they studied last night. What type of data is collected?

answer.text: Numerical, because minutes measure an amount of time

feedback.text: Minutes can be compared, ordered, and averaged because they measure time.

answer.text: Categorical, because the values are labels

feedback.text: Minutes are measured amounts, not labels. Use what the numbers mean in context.

answer.text: Categorical, because each student gives one answer

feedback.text: One answer per student does not make data categorical.

answer.text: Neither, because time is not data

feedback.text: Time can be recorded as data when it answers a statistical question.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L01_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A class records each student's favorite movie genre. What type of data is collected?

answer.text: Numerical, because the class can count responses

feedback.text: Counting responses later does not change the original variable.

answer.text: Numerical, because every response can be listed

feedback.text: Listing responses does not make them quantities.

answer.text: Both numerical and categorical

feedback.text: The original variable is a category, not a measurement.

answer.text: Categorical, because genre is a label or group

feedback.text: Movie genre names groups rather than measured amounts.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L01_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.2

Data table:

StudentID numberWhat the value names
A10458Identifier label
B20731Identifier label
C31984Identifier label

Use the table to decide whether the numbers measure an amount or name a category.

A data table lists student ID numbers. How should the ID numbers be classified?

answer.text: Numerical, because the values use digits

feedback.text: Digits alone do not make data numerical.

answer.text: Numerical, because the numbers can be ordered

feedback.text: ID order usually does not represent a measured amount.

answer.text: Categorical, because the numbers are labels

feedback.text: Student ID numbers identify people; arithmetic with the IDs is not meaningful.

answer.text: Both, because every label is also a number

feedback.text: A value used as a label should be treated as categorical data.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L01_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display is usually appropriate for counts of students in each favorite app category?

answer.text: Bar chart

feedback.text: A bar chart compares counts across categories.

answer.text: Histogram

feedback.text: Histograms show numerical intervals, not category labels.

answer.text: Dot plot

feedback.text: Dot plots are usually used for numerical values.

answer.text: Scatterplot

feedback.text: Scatterplots show relationships between two numerical variables.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L01_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.2

A display shows the number of pets owned by each student. Why is this numerical data?

answer.text: Because pets are animals

feedback.text: The context is pets, but the variable is the number owned.

answer.text: Because the values are counts that can be compared and summarized

feedback.text: Number of pets is a count, so comparing or finding a mean is meaningful.

answer.text: Because every survey answer is numerical

feedback.text: Not every survey answer is numerical.

answer.text: Because the display has a title

feedback.text: A title helps interpretation but does not determine data type.
